newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: INTERVIEW-Data does not contract RBNZ view - Orr.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Data does not contract RBNZ view - Orr.

text.p: Recent economic data did not contradict the Reserve Bank'S view of the New Zealand economy although it remained on 'creditwatch' regarding economic indicators, RB Chief Manager Economics Adrian Orr told Reuters on Thursday.
"But there has been nothing that has derailed our view of where the economy is. That is not to say it does not remain on creditwatch," he said.
"Certainly, the data we have seen so far does not contradict our view."

Orr said March quarter GDP data showing a 0.5 fall in growth was somewhat misleading because Easter was not included in the quarter as ususal and the Department of Statistics had not adjusted for that.
"We are continuing to look at all data and the negative GDP data, which seems to have sent people into a tailspin, you have to be very careful when looking at that negative," he said.
"There is a positive adjustment to be made to it, which is a significant adjustment. When you see the June quarter there will be a bounce back from that.
"Once you do that you do get the kickback in the June quarter. It was not as soft as the minus 0.5 (percent) points to."
He said June quarter inflation data was exactly on the bank's forecasts at 0.3 percent for the quarter and 1.49 percent for the year.

"The CPI was bang on, the GDP has sent these negative vibes but there is this (Easter) factor and other one-offs. The other indicators are saying we stay on 'creditwatch' with the rest of the indicators as they come out," he said.
He said if the retail sales for June came out flat then sales for the June quarter would be positive.

Commenting on the fact that the financial markets had kept monetary conditions softer than the Reserve Bank's desired level, Orr said: "The most positive thing you could say is that financial markets look at the data as it comes out and think 'what does it mean for inflation 12 to 18 months ahead. In other words, they are playing the game and they have proved to be able to do that successfully in the past."
The MCI at 764 was 61 basis points in interest rate terms outside the bank's desired level shortly before Orr spoke.
